title: fix(stats): median Tinybird cost so flat-rate preflight isn't 402'd
author: iotserver24
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #12747

## Why the estimate was ~33.34 (not 0.01)

`checkBalance()` reads Tinybird `public_model_stats.avg_cost_usd`, which was a **7-day mean** of `total_price`.

Request-priced community images used to bill:

`completionImagePrice * OpenAI output_tokens`

For `vendouple/zimage` that is **0.01 × ~3334 ≈ 33.34** — the number in the 402. Billing already logs `{ completionImageTokens: 1 }` for `imagePricing !== "tokens"`, so **new** events are ~0.01. The **mean** stays poisoned until old rows age out, and token-priced models have the same outlier problem with no flat rate to fall back on.

## Change

1. **Tinybird** `public_model_stats.pipe`: `avgIf` → `medianIf` (column name stays `avg_cost_usd`). Typical charge, not a few misbilled rows.
2. **Preflight** still uses Tinybird. It only uses the defined per-request price when Tinybird is missing or **>10×** that price (clearly garbage). Token-priced models keep Tinybird.

Needs a Tinybird `deployment create` on staging then prod for the pipe to go live.

## Tests

- community flat-rate 0.01 + Tinybird 33.34 + budget 5 → allowed (Tinybird treated as outlier)
- same model + Tinybird 0.012 → trusts Tinybird
- same model + budget 0.005 → 402 quoting `~0.0100`
- `openai` still uses Tinybird

`npx vitest run src/byop-markup.test.ts` — 22 passed.

gist.headline: Outliers leave the hive
gist.blurb: A few ancient, wildly overpriced image records were spooking the balance checker. The hive now uses the typical charge and knows when a flat-rate flower is just a flat-rate flower.
gist.summary: Replaced Tinybird's 7-day mean cost with a median and made flat-rate image preflight fall back to the defined per-request price when Tinybird reports an estimate more than 10× higher, while token-priced models continue using Tinybird.
gist.impact: Community image requests such as vendouple/zimage at $0.01 are no longer incorrectly blocked by a stale ~$33.34 estimate, while genuinely low budgets still receive an accurate 402 quoting about $0.0100.

A friendly CRT monitor robot compares a median stack of small price pebbles against the obvious outlier, representing robust Tinybird statistics and fair preflight access.
